messages:
Maya (CS): Hey team, Acme onboarding — seeing intermittent 403s right after our JS SDK bootstrap. They report auth failures for a few hundred ms, then things recover. No change on their app code. Any ideas?
Ravi (SRE): Can you paste the client-side logs and the relay logs from our auth proxy? Also what SDK version are they on?
Maya (CS): SDK v1.4.1 (browser). Client log snippet: 
```
[2025-05-08T15:12:03.123Z] SDK bootstrap start session=abc123
[2025-05-08T15:12:03.210Z] fetch /auth/token 200 (latency=45ms)
[2025-05-08T15:12:03.225Z] request /inference 403 {"code":"invalid_token","msg":"aud mismatch"}
[2025-05-08T15:12:03.320Z] fetch /auth/token 200 (latency=38ms)
[2025-05-08T15:12:03.330Z] request /inference 200
```
Maya (CS): Relay (our edge) shows a flurry of token-exchange requests around the same second, then 403s.
Jorge (SDK): "aud mismatch" + double token fetch pattern smells like a token rotation race during parallel bootstrap. Browser clients fire multiple preflight/auth calls if init is concurrent (e.g., multiple tabs). If token TTL is very short and our auth proxy returns different kid/aud metadata briefly, you can get a mismatch.
Luisa (Eng): Also check for clock skew on their host or our proxy returning tokens with a very tight nbf/window. Small skew + immediate reuse can trigger aud/nbf checks.
Maya (CS): Customer says they open multiple tabs and rapid replay on load balancer. They said their system clock is OK.
Ravi (SRE): Two quick checks: 1) what is the token TTL and rotation interval from their tenant config? 2) are clients doing a hard fetch on every SDK init (no cache)?
Maya (CS): TTL=30s, rotation interval=25s (reported by tenant admin). Client bootstraps don't cache between tabs.
Jorge (SDK): That's aggressive. 25s rotate + no client cache + multi-tab bootstrap = token fanout. If one tab got a token A and another got token B with slightly different claims, downstream services that did a cached audience check might reject B briefly. Also if they hit different auth nodes during rotation, kid mismatch possible.
Luisa (Eng): Short-term mitigation: 1) bump TTL to 120s or 180s for the onboarding tenant, 2) enable client-side session cache in SDK (we have a flag `reuse_session:true` in v1.4.2), 3) add small jitter on client retry (exponential backoff with +/- 100-250ms).
Maya (CS): Customer can change TTL? They are willing. I told them about SDK flag but they are on v1.4.1.
Jorge (SDK): We shipped `reuse_session:true` in v1.4.2 that stores ephemeral token in localSession keyed by origin — avoids multi-tab re-fetch. Recommend upgrade to v1.4.2. Also deploy a temporary server-side token grace window within auth proxy: allow tokens with aud of previous token for 1s during rotation.
Ravi (SRE): I'll add a 1s grace on auth-proxy audience checks for that tenant and enable logging to trace the `kid` changes.
deploy-bot: deploy started: auth-proxy/2025-05-08T15:30Z -> canary to prod-edge (tags: grace-window).
Maya (CS): I'll coordinate upgrade window with Acme; prefer same-day so they can test.
Luisa (Eng): If they can't upgrade quickly, we can temporarily increase TTL on their tenant and enable server-side grace. Both combined should eliminate the 403 windows.
Maya (CS): Action items: (1) Ravi enable 1s aud grace (in progress), (2) Luisa confirm SDK flag docs and patch notes for v1.4.2, (3) Customer to bump TTL to 120s and test multi-tab start. I'll follow up after their morning test.
Jorge (SDK): Also attach quick diagnostic snippet for them to paste in console to surface token headers: 
```js
// paste in console to show cached token info
console.log(window.__RW_SESSION__); // SDK session store (if present)
fetch('/auth/token').then(r=>r.json()).then(console.log);
```
Maya (CS): Thanks — sending that to Acme now. Will update thread when they report back. :thumbsup:
